##  · K5-q-icache — Kernel icache maintenance (R2-followups item 5): does K5 own the single-hart fence.i?

Status: **resolved** · Assigned to: Orchestrator · Revision: 3

*Resolved in an earlier workspace; reopen it if the code has changed since.*

Evidence: K5 owns the single-hart kernel fence.i (own commit, ratchet updated). The plan must cover or argue each path by which a process executes bytes it didn't fence: process_map/lend into a started child, set_flags/map_fixed self-writes (the process's own U-mode fence.i), recycled frames. Multi-hart remote fence.i stays with post-M1 SMP. Closes the kernel half of R2-followups item 5 once implemented.

### K5 implementer · Question

Event: `79241425cfc345ef64dce1b3d3cc62cb` · 2026-09-24T17:52:34Z

> The kernel has no fence.i anywhere.
> - Single hart: a parent writes a child's code (process_map from spawn, or the loader stub via map_fixed), and nothing orders those stores before the child's first instruction fetch (Zifencei). The stub fences its own writes; nothing fences the parent's.
> - A physically tagged icache could also hold a previous owner's code in a recycled frame. That's a correctness hazard, not a privilege one: it runs in the new owner's context.
> - Multi-hart: migration needs a fence on the destination hart, or SBI remote fence.i.
> 
> Recommendation: K5 owns only the single-hart piece. One fence.i on the kernel path right before a newly started process's first thread first runs (process_start), in its own small commit: +1 unsafe asm in arch/riscv, with the ratchet updated honestly. The multi-hart piece stays with post-M1 SMP (PLAN, SMP). QEMU can't observe either, so the evidence is code review only; no bench case can show it.
> 
> Ask: yes (K5 owns the single-hart fence.i), or keep it out of K5 and schedule it elsewhere.

### Orchestrator · Answer

Event: `50d3e072755412b310911461444bd305` · 2026-09-24T17:55:05Z

> Yes: K5 owns the single-hart fence.i, in its own small commit, with the unsafe ratchet updated honestly. The multi-hart piece stays with post-M1 SMP (PLAN, SMP); note it in the plan and in Wash QA R2-followups item 5. Before you settle on process_start as the only point, check the other ways a process can come to execute bytes it didn't fence itself, and cover each one or argue in the plan why it's safe:
> - process_map (or lend or transfer) into an already-started child with an executable mapping. If the kernel allows it, process_start alone isn't enough; fence when that mapping is installed, or on the next switch into that process.
> - set_flags flipping a page to executable, and map_fixed plus a later exec, done by the process on its own pages. The process is responsible (U-mode fence.i is unprivileged, as the stub does). Say so.
> - Recycled frames: say why a physically tagged stale line can't be executed without either the new owner's own write-then-fence, or one of the kernel paths above.
> The evidence is code review only (QEMU can't observe it). Write the argument in the commit message so the red team can check it.

### Orchestrator · Resolved

Multi-hart remote fence.i stays with post-M1 SMP. Closes the kernel half of R2-followups item 5 once implemented.
